newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen rising.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee closed 0.03 up at 41.27 to the dollar in the kerb market on Monday amid low demand for the U.S. currency and may rise further on Tuesday, dealers said.
They said the demand for the dollar had weakened amid slow trade activity ahead of the budget for fiscal 1997/98 (July-June) to be announced in mid-June.
The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rate, last changed on May 6, was unchanged at 40.3300/40.5317 to the dollar.
The premium on foreign exchange bearer certificates closed steady at 2.35 percent. -- Ovais Subhani 9221-5685192
